title: Late Fees Arising from a Duplicate Posting — Northgate Card Treatment of Fees Charged in Error and Above the Ceiling
content:
**Fees charged in error.** On **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** accounts, for the late fee recorded for the statement that first showed the disputed posting of a duplicate-posting dispute settled for the cardholder, and only where the late fee carried by the error is above zero, the part charged in error or above the dispute-adjusted minimum is credited inside the duplicate-posting final credit instead of being reversed as a fee; where the late fee carried by the error is nothing, and for every other fee, a fee charged in error, or above the minimum-payment ceiling, is reversed in full as a billing error or for the excess as a regulatory cap correction.

**Dispute-adjusted minimum.** The dispute-adjusted minimum is worked out in two steps: first the tier's minimum payment percentage of the disputed amount, rounded half up to the cent, is taken off the minimum payment due printed on the statement that first showed the disputed posting, which still included that amount because the notice came after the statement closed; then, where what remains is below the tier's minimum payment floor, the floor is used instead. The tier's minimum payment percentage is 1% on the Northgate Secured Card, Northgate Store Card, Northgate Mastercard and Northgate World Mastercard and 2% on the Northgate Business Store Card and Northgate Business Mastercard; the tier's minimum payment floor is 30.00 USD on the Northgate Secured Card and 40.00 USD on every other card.

**Standing late fee.** The standing late fee is the late fee recorded for the statement that first showed the disputed posting, less every reversal already posted against that fee, never less than zero.

**Late fee carried by the error.** It is set by that standing late fee:

1. where the standing late fee is above zero, the dispute being settled is the only billing-error dispute on a transaction that statement first showed, its notice was received after that statement's closing date and on or before its payment due date and the payments recorded against that statement reach the dispute-adjusted minimum, it is the whole standing late fee;
2. where the standing late fee is above zero, the dispute being settled is the only billing-error dispute on a transaction that statement first showed, its notice was received after that statement's closing date and on or before its payment due date, the payments recorded against that statement fall short of the dispute-adjusted minimum and the standing late fee is above the dispute-adjusted minimum, it is the standing late fee less the dispute-adjusted minimum;
3. in every other case it is nothing.

The statement that first showed the disputed posting is the statement whose closing date the dispute records. A payment is recorded against the statement whose balance it pays, and the payments recorded against a statement are all the payment entries that carry that statement's closing date.

| Standing fee above zero; only billing-error dispute on that statement; notice after closing and on or before the due date | Payments recorded against the statement | Standing fee compared with the adjusted minimum | Late fee carried by the error |
|---|---|---|---|
| all hold | reach the adjusted minimum | any | the whole standing fee |
| all hold | fall short | above | standing fee less the adjusted minimum |
| all hold | fall short | not above | nothing |
| any of them fails | any | any | nothing |

## Hypothetical worked figures

A consumer tier with a 1% minimum payment percentage and a 40.00 floor; printed minimum 61.00; disputed amount 150.00. Step one: 1% of 150.00 is 1.50, and 61.00 less 1.50 leaves 59.50. Step two: 59.50 is not below the 40.00 floor, so the dispute-adjusted minimum is 59.50. With a standing late fee of 32.00, notice received after closing and before the due date, and payments of 59.50 recorded against the statement, the late fee carried by the error is the whole 32.00. On another hypothetical account where the adjusted minimum falls to the 40.00 floor, the standing fee is 43.00 and the payments fall short of 40.00, it is 43.00 less 40.00, that is 3.00.
